title: Northern Harrier — hunting in snow
subtitle: A northern harrier in low flight over snow at Barr Lake, Colorado, talons reaching forward to grasp some brush. Bright, almost featureless snow surfaces alongside finely barred wing and tail feathers give noise-reduction tools a wide tonal range to handle.
editor_note: I disagree with darwain on this one — I prefer the Topaz Photo versions to DxO.
exif_summary: OM-1 with M.150-400mm F4.5 TC + MC-14 at 700mm, 1/2000s at f/8, ISO 500

images.title: RAW
images.caption: Original RAW image, which is quite soft.

critique.text: As the baseline original RAW, this image exhibits noticeable overall softness, lacking fine detail in the hawk's feathers, face, and the dry brush below. There is a moderate amount of luminance and color noise visible in the snowy background and the shadow areas of the bird. It serves as a good reference point showing that the subject requires significant sharpening and noise reduction to achieve a crisp final result, though it maintains a completely natural, artifact-free baseline.

images.title: DxO PureRAW 6
images.caption: Dxo using DxO DeepPrime wD3 with Lens Sharpness Optimization increased to 200

critique.text: This DxO PureRAW version strikes the best balance of the entire set. The DeepPRIME XD3 engine completely removes the noise in the snow while extracting an impressive amount of fine sharpness in the hawk's feathers, eye, and the dry brush, far surpassing the original RAW. It effectively sharpens the soft original while managing to avoid the heavy waxy artifacts seen in the Topaz edits, resulting in a crisp, natural, and highly dynamic final image.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with default noise reduction ans subject sharpening using lens blur at setting of 50

critique.text: This version applies Topaz Photo without the upsize. It effectively cleans up the noise in the snow while dramatically improving the sharpness of the hawk compared to the soft original RAW. The details in the feathers and talons are much crisper and the subject isolation is excellent. While it still exhibits minor waxy artifacts from the AI sharpening, it remains highly impactful and looks noticeably more natural than the 2x upscaled image.

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom AI Denoise at default settings

critique.text: Lightroom's AI Denoise does an excellent job of smoothly eliminating the noise from the snowy background without introducing artificial textures. However, because it relies primarily on noise reduction at default settings rather than aggressive subject sharpening, the hawk remains quite soft, very similar to the original RAW. It is a wonderfully clean image, but the trade-off is that it lacks the necessary sharpness to make the main subject truly stand out.

images.title: Topaz Photo 2x upsized
images.caption: This uses Topaz Photo with noise reduction, subject sharpening with lens blur, and 2x upsizing

critique.text: Using Topaz Photo with a 2x upscale, this version successfully eliminates the background noise seen in the RAW and introduces an aggressive level of sharpness. However, it suffers from typical AI over-sharpening artifacts; the feathers appear somewhat waxy and crunchy, losing natural texture. While the subject pops significantly more than the original RAW, the heavy-handed sharpening and artificial-looking details in the wings detract slightly from its overall realism.

images.title: ON1 RAW
images.caption: ON1 RAW with NoNoise and TackSharp

critique.text: Processed with ON1 RAW, this image struggles to recover the missing sharpness of the original RAW. While background noise is reasonably reduced compared to the original, the TackSharp application leaves the hawk looking somewhat muddy and smeared rather than crisp. It lacks the defining edge detail in the eye, talons, and feathers seen in the Topaz or DxO versions, making the overall processing feel ineffective for this specific file.
